title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 25 (Document containing offer of securities for sale to be deemed prospectus)

content.overview: Section 25 provides that where a company allots or agrees to allot any securities of the company with a view to all or any of those securities being offered for sale to the public, any document by which the offer for sale to the public is made shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be a prospectus issued by the company. All enactments and rules as to contents of prospectus and liability for mis-statements or omissions apply with the modifications in sub-sections (3) and (4). There is a rebuttable presumption that an allotment or agreement to allot was made with a view to public sale if an offer for sale is made within six months after the allotment or agreement, or if at the date of the offer the whole consideration to be received by the company had not been received.
content.glance: Allotment with a view to public offer for sale → offer document deemed a prospectus; six-month / unpaid-consideration presumption; s.26 modifications; persons named as directors treated as directors for liability.
content.study:
Section 25 prevents avoidance of prospectus rules by using an offer-for-sale structure.

Statutory test
1. Deeming rule: company allots or agrees to allot securities with a view to all or any being offered for sale to the public → any document by which the offer for sale is made is deemed a prospectus issued by the company.
2. Application of prospectus law: contents and liability rules apply with modifications in sub-sections (3) and (4).
3. Presumption (unless contrary proved): allotment/agreement with a view to public sale is evidenced if (a) offer for sale within six months after allotment or agreement, or (b) at the date of the offer the whole consideration to be received by the company had not been received.
4. Additional content when s.26 is applied: net amount of consideration received or to be received by the company; time and place at which the contract under which the securities have been or are to be allotted may be inspected.
5. Liability adaptation: persons named in the document as directors or proposed directors of the company are treated as directors of the company for the purposes of liability.

Boundary
Section 25 is about characterisation (when an offer-for-sale document is a prospectus). Section 26 is about what a prospectus must contain and the formalities of dating, signing and filing.

sections.heading: Deeming rule
sections.body: Where a company allots or agrees to allot securities with a view to all or any of them being offered for sale to the public, any document by which the offer for sale is made is deemed to be a prospectus issued by the company.

sections.heading: Presumption
sections.body: Unless the contrary is proved, an allotment or agreement to allot is evidence of a view to public sale if an offer for sale is made within six months after the allotment or agreement, or if at the date of the offer the whole consideration to be received by the company had not been received.

sections.heading: Modifications when section 26 applies
sections.body: Section 26 as applied requires, in addition, statement of the net amount of consideration received or to be received by the company and the time and place at which the allotment contract may be inspected.

sections.heading: Liability adaptation
sections.body: Persons named in the document as directors or proposed directors of the company are treated as directors of the company for the purposes of liability under prospectus law.

provisions.title: Document containing offer of securities for sale to be deemed prospectus

examples.title: Offer for sale after allotment
examples.body: A company allots shares to an intermediary who within six months offers them to the public. The offer document is deemed a prospectus under section 25; the six-month presumption applies unless the contrary is proved.

hypotheticals.question: Can a company avoid prospectus rules by allotting to a middleman who then sells to the public?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 25 deems the offer-for-sale document a prospectus where the allotment was with a view to public sale. The six-month and unpaid-consideration presumptions assist proof of that view.

distinctions.title: Deemed prospectus (s. 25) vs content of prospectus (s. 26)
distinctions.left: When an offer-for-sale document is treated as a prospectus
distinctions.right: What a prospectus must contain and formalities

misconceptions.trap: Only a document formally labelled prospectus attracts prospectus law.
misconceptions.correction: Section 25 deems certain offer-for-sale documents to be prospectuses regardless of label.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 25 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify allotment or agreement to allot with a view to public sale. II. Apply the deeming rule and any presumption. III. Apply prospectus duties with the statutory modifications. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Note the six-month and unpaid-consideration presumptions.
